rows.label: 前缀 (老-)

lesson.title: 老-: a prefix for familiar names, birth order and some nouns
lesson.summary: 老 before a surname makes a friendly form of address, before a number gives birth order among siblings, and is a fixed part of some nouns such as 老师 and 老虎.
pattern: 老 + surname
老 + 大 / 二 / 三 …
老 + noun root (老师, 老虎, 老家)
body: 老 (lǎo) is a prefix with three common jobs. Before a one-syllable surname it makes a friendly, familiar way to address or mention someone of your age or older: 老王, 老张, 老李. Before 大, 二, 三 and so on it gives the order of children in a family: 老大 is the eldest, 老二 the second, 老三 the third. In some nouns it is simply part of the word and adds no idea of age: 老师 (teacher), 老虎 (tiger, even a baby one), 老家 (hometown), 老板 (boss).
The contrast example uses 小 (Level 1): 小李. 小 + surname is the friendly form for someone younger than you; 老 + surname is for someone your age or older. Both attach to the surname only.
Common mistake: putting 老 before a full name or a given name (老王小明). Say 老王, or the full name without 老.

rows.label: 后缀 (-家, -子, -员)

lesson.title: Suffixes -家, -子 and -员: experts, everyday nouns and staff
lesson.summary: -家 marks an expert or artist, -子 is a common noun ending, and -员 marks a person who does a job or belongs to a group.
pattern: field + 家 (画家, 科学家)
root + 子 (桌子, 帽子, 儿子)
activity + 员 (服务员, 运动员)
body: A suffix attaches to the back of a word. 家 (jiā) after a field names a recognised expert or artist: 画家 (painter), 科学家 (scientist), 音乐家 (musician), 作家 (writer). 子 (zi, neutral tone) is a common ending of everyday nouns: 桌子, 椅子, 帽子, 儿子, 孩子, 筷子. 员 (yuán) names a person who does a job or is a member: 服务员 (waiter), 运动员 (athlete), 演员 (actor), 售货员 (shop assistant).
The contrast example uses 们 (Level 1), which makes a person-noun plural: 演员们. 们 can follow a noun that already has 员 or 家; it adds the idea of many people, not a job.
Common mistake: swapping the suffixes. 家 is for a respected expert (科学家, not 科学员); 员 is for a staff member or player (服务员, not 服务家).

rows.label: 方位名词 (东, 南, 西, 北, 北方, 东方, 南方, 西方, 中间)

lesson.title: Compass words: 东 南 西 北, 北方 南方 东方 西方, and 中间
lesson.summary: 东, 南, 西 and 北 combine with 边 for a side of a place and with 方 for a direction or region; 中间 means in the middle or between.
pattern: N + 的 + 东边 / 南边 / 西边 / 北边
东方 / 南方 / 西方 / 北方 (+ 的 + N)
在 + A 和 B + 中间
body: 东 (dōng, east), 南 (nán, south), 西 (xī, west) and 北 (běi, north) are bound words. After a place noun they take 边: 学校的东边, 城市的北边. With 方 they name a direction or a large region: 北方 (the north of a country), 南方, 东方 (the east; also the East), 西方 (the west; also the West, Western countries). Compound directions put east or west first: 东南, 西北.
中间 (zhōngjiān) is the middle of something or the space between two things: 在超市和书店中间. 中 alone does not work as a place word here.

The contrast example uses 右 (Level 2): 往右走. 左 and 右 give direction relative to the speaker, while the compass words give a fixed direction. Common mistake: using a bare compass word or 方 for a side of a small place (中国的北, 超市东方). Use 北方 for a region and 东边 for the side of a building.

rows.label: 能愿动词 (需要, 该, 应该, 愿意, 得)

lesson.title: Modal verbs 需要, 应该/该, 愿意 and 得 (děi)
lesson.summary: 需要 says something is needed, 应该 and 该 say what is right or expected, 愿意 says someone is willing, and 得 (děi) says you have to.
pattern: A + 需要 + V / N
A + 应该 / 该 / 得 + V
A + (很) 愿意 + V
body: 需要 (xūyào) means need. It can take a verb (你需要多休息) or a noun (我需要一张地图), and its subject can be a thing: 这个问题需要好好想一想. 应该 (yīnggāi) and the shorter, more spoken 该 (gāi) say what is right or expected: 你应该早点儿告诉我, 你不该这么晚才回家. 愿意 (yuànyì) says a person is willing, and it can take 很: 我很愿意帮助你.
得 (děi) is spoken and means have to: 我得早点儿睡. It is written like the particle 得 (de) but read děi and stands before a verb. Its negative is 不用 (no need), not 不得.

The contrast example uses 会 (Level 1) for a prediction: 明天会下雨吗？ 会 can talk about weather; 愿意 cannot, because weather has no will. Common mistake: using 愿意 with a thing as subject, or saying 不得 for no need to.

rows.label: 离合词 (放假, 见面, 结婚, 洗澡; 离开, 完成, 分开)

lesson.title: Separable verbs: 放假 见面 结婚 洗澡 and 离开 完成 分开
lesson.summary: Verb-object words like 见面 open up for 了, 过, a measure or 的; verb-complement words like 离开 open up for 得 or 不.
pattern: V + 了 / 过 / 个 / number + measure + O (见过一次面)
V + 得 / 不 + C (离不开, 完得成)
跟 + person + 见面
body: Verb-object separable words have a verb part and an object part. 放假 (have a holiday), 见面 (meet), 结婚 (marry) and 洗澡 (take a bath) let other words go between the two parts: 放了一个星期的假, 见过一次面, 是去年结的婚, 洗个澡. Because the word already contains an object, it cannot take another one: say 跟他见面, not 见面他.
Verb-complement words have a verb and a result: 离开 (leave), 完成 (finish), 分开 (separate). 得 or 不 goes between the parts to say can or cannot: 离得开 / 离不开, 完得成 / 完不成, 分不开.

The contrast example uses 帮助, an ordinary verb that takes an object directly: 他经常帮助我. 帮忙 (Level 2) is separable and cannot: 他经常帮忙我 is wrong, 他经常帮我的忙 is right. Common mistake: putting the object or the measure after the whole word, as in 见面他 or 见面一次.

rows.label: 疑问代词 (怎样)

lesson.title: 怎样: asking how, in what way and what kind
lesson.summary: 怎样 asks about manner before a verb, about a state at the end of a sentence, and about kind before 的 + noun.
pattern: A + 怎样 + V？
A + 怎样？
一个怎样的 + N？
body: 怎样 (zěnyàng) is a slightly more formal partner of 怎么 and 怎么样. Before a verb it asks how something is done: 这个字怎样写？ 我们应该怎样学好汉语？ At the end of a sentence it asks about a state or an opinion: 你最近身体怎样？ 你看这件衣服怎样？ Before 的 and a noun it asks what kind: 他是一个怎样的人？
The contrast example uses 怎么 for surprise or why: 你怎么又迟到了？ 怎么 can ask why or how come; 怎样 only asks how or what kind, so 你怎样又迟到了 is wrong.
Common mistake: using 怎么 before 的 (一个怎么的人). Before 的 + noun use 怎样 or 怎么样.

rows.label: 疑问代词的非疑问用法 (任指, 不定指)

lesson.title: Question words without a question: anything, anyone, anywhere and something
lesson.summary: A question word followed by 都 or 也 means any or every (什么都, 谁都); the same word twice links two clauses; and in a statement a question word can mean something, somewhere or someone.
pattern: QW + 都 / 也 + (不 / 没) + V
…QW…, 就…QW…
V + 点儿 + 什么 / 在哪儿 + V
body: A question word does not always ask a question. Before 都 or 也 it means any or every, and with 不 or 没 it means nothing, nobody or nowhere: 他什么都不想吃, 谁都知道这件事, 周末我哪儿也没去, 怎么走都可以. The question word comes before 都 or 也, in front of the verb.

The same question word can appear in two clauses, linked by 就, and the two refer to the same thing: 你想吃什么就吃什么 (eat whatever you want). In a statement a question word can also stand for something, somewhere or someone not named: 吃点儿什么吧, 我好像在哪儿见过他.

The contrast example is an ordinary question: 你周末去哪儿了？ Here 哪儿 asks for a place and needs an answer. With 都 or 也, in the double pattern, or in a statement, the question word asks nothing. Common mistake: leaving the question word after the verb (我都不想吃什么); say 我什么都不想吃.

rows.label: 人称代词 (别人, 咱们)

lesson.title: 别人 (other people) and 咱们 (we, including you)
lesson.summary: 别人 means other people and stands alone as a pronoun; 咱们 means we and always includes the person you are speaking to.
pattern: 别人 (+ 的 + N)
V + 别人
咱们 + V (+ 吧)
body: 别人 (biéren) means other people, anyone except the person in question. It works like a pronoun: as subject (别人都走了), as object (他总是想着别人) and before 的 (别人的东西). 咱们 (zánmen) means we and always includes the listener; it is common in spoken northern Chinese: 咱们一起去吃饭吧, 咱们班.
The contrast example uses 我们 (Level 1): 老师，我们先走了，您慢慢吃. The speakers leave and the teacher stays, so the listener is not included and 咱们 is wrong; 我们 can include or exclude the listener.
Common mistake: using 别的 for people on its own (别的都走了 for other people left). 别的 needs a noun or means other things; for people say 别人 or 别的人.

rows.label: 指示代词 (别的, 其他)

lesson.title: 别的 and 其他: other things, other people
lesson.summary: 别的 and 其他 both mean other; 别的 can stand alone for other things, and 其他 often means the rest of a known group.
pattern: 别的 + N / 别的 (alone)
其他 + N / 其他的
除了 A，其他 + N + 都…
body: 别的 (bié de) means other. It goes before a noun (别的颜色) or stands alone for other things (你还想要别的吗？). 其他 (qítā) also means other and usually points to the rest of a known group: 其他同学都回家了, 除了小王，其他人都来了. Used alone it takes 的: 其他的都没买.
The contrast example uses 别人 (row 7): 我没有把这件事告诉别人. For other people, 别人 is the pronoun; 别的 and 其他 need a noun such as 人 to mean people.
Common mistake: putting 别人 before a noun as if it meant other (别人颜色). Use 别的颜色 or 其他颜色.

rows.label: 名量词 (把, 双, 张, 种, 层, 封, 页, 辆, 节, 所, 班, 段, 头, 句)

lesson.title: Measure words for objects, places, vehicles and speech: 把 双 张 种 层 封 页 辆 节 所 班 段 头 句
lesson.summary: Each measure word goes between a number or 这/那 and a noun, and fits a kind of thing: 把 for things with handles, 张 for flat things, 辆 for vehicles, 句 for sentences.
pattern: number / 这 / 那 + measure + N
一把雨伞, 两张票, 几辆车, 一句话
body: 把 (bǎ) is for things you hold by a handle: 一把雨伞, 一把椅子. 双 (shuāng) is a pair: 一双鞋, 一双筷子. 张 (zhāng) is for flat things: 一张票, 一张纸, 一张桌子. 种 (zhǒng) is a kind: 这种楼. 层 (céng) is a floor or layer: 六层. 封 (fēng) is for letters, 页 (yè) for pages: 一封三页的信. 辆 (liàng) is for vehicles: 几辆车.

节 (jié) counts class periods: 这节课. 所 (suǒ) is for schools and hospitals: 那所大学. 班 (bān) counts scheduled runs of a bus, train or plane: 下一班车. 段 (duàn) is a stretch or section: 这段路, 这段话. 头 (tóu) is for large animals: 一头牛. 句 (jù) counts sentences: 一句话.

The contrast example uses 位 (Level 2), the polite measure for people: 一位新同学. In the same sentence 班 is a noun (a class of students), not the measure word for runs of a bus. Common mistake: using 个 or the wrong measure for vehicles and animals (一个车, 一张牛); say 一辆车, 一头牛.

rows.label: 名量词 (公斤, 斤, 角, 毛, 刻, 米; 借用 碗, 盘)

lesson.title: Units and borrowed measures: 公斤 斤 角 毛 刻 米, 碗 盘
lesson.summary: 公斤 and 斤 weigh, 角 and 毛 count tenths of a yuan, 刻 is a quarter of an hour, 米 is a metre, and 碗 and 盘 borrow a bowl and a plate as measures.
pattern: number + 公斤 / 斤 / 米 (+ N)
…块 / 元 + number + 毛 / 角
number + 碗 / 盘 + N
body: 公斤 (gōngjīn) is a kilogram and 斤 (jīn) is half a kilogram, the usual unit in Chinese markets: 两斤苹果. 米 (mǐ) is a metre; height is said 一米八 (1.8 metres). 刻 (kè) is a quarter of an hour: 三点一刻 (3:15), 三点三刻 (3:45).
Money: 1 元 = 10 角 = 100 分. In speech 块 replaces 元 and 毛 replaces 角: 三块五毛 in speech, 三元五角 in writing. Borrowed measures use a container: 一碗米饭, 一盘饺子.

The contrast example uses 分钟 (Level 1): 二十分钟. 分 counts minutes and goes with any number; 刻 only counts quarters, so you say 一刻 or 三刻, never 二十刻. Common mistake: mixing spoken and written money words (三元五毛). Keep 块 with 毛 and 元 with 角.

rows.label: 动量词 (口, 回, 遍, 声)

lesson.title: Measures for actions: 口, 回, 遍 and 声
lesson.summary: After a verb, 口 counts mouthfuls, 回 counts times, 遍 counts complete runs from start to end, and 声 counts sounds or short spoken words.
pattern: V + (了) + number + 口 / 回 / 遍 / 声 (+ O)
V + pronoun + 一声
body: A verbal measure counts how many times an action happens. 口 (kǒu) counts mouthfuls: 喝了一口茶, 尝了一口. 回 (huí) is a spoken word for times, like 次: 我去过两回. 遍 (biàn) counts a complete run from beginning to end: 读三遍, 看了两遍. 声 (shēng) counts a sound or a short word: 笑了一声, 跟我说一声 (let me know).
The number and measure follow the verb (and 了 or 过). A noun object usually comes after them (喝了一口茶), but a pronoun comes before them: 叫了我一声.

The contrast example uses 次 (Level 2): 游三次泳. 次 simply counts occurrences; 遍 adds the idea of doing the whole thing through, so 游三遍泳 is wrong. Common mistake: using 遍 for going somewhere (去过两遍上海); say 两次 or 两回.

rows.label: 量词重叠 (个个, 张张)

lesson.title: Doubled measure words: 个个, 张张 mean every single one
lesson.summary: A doubled measure word such as 个个 or 张张 means every one of them; it stands before the verb, usually with 都.
pattern: N + MM + 都 + predicate
个个 / 张张 / 本本 / 样样 / 天天
body: Doubling a measure word gives the meaning every single one: 同学个个都很努力, 照片张张都很好看. The same works with other measures: 本本 (every book), 样样 (every kind), 件件 (every piece). Time words double the same way: 天天 (every day). The doubled measure comes after the thing it counts and before the verb, and it usually goes with 都.
The contrast example uses 每 (Level 2): 每个人都有自己的爱好. 每 needs a measure word after it and goes before the noun; the doubled measure replaces 每 + measure and follows the noun.
Common mistake: putting the doubled measure after the verb (我喜欢张张照片). Say 这些照片我张张都喜欢 or 每张照片我都喜欢.

rows.label: 程度副词 (比较, 更, 还, 越)

lesson.title: Degree adverbs that compare: 比较, 更, 还 and 越
lesson.summary: 比较 means fairly or relatively, 更 means even more, 还 means even more in a 比 sentence or passably before 不错, and 越……越 means the more … the more.
pattern: A + 比较 / 更 + Adj / V
A + 比 B + 还 + Adj；A + 还 + 不错 / 可以
A + 越 + V + 越 + Adj
body: 比较 (bǐjiào) gives a mild degree, fairly or relatively: 今天比较冷. 更 (gèng) means even more and implies a comparison with something already mentioned: 我喜欢春天，更喜欢秋天. 还 (hái) as a degree adverb has two uses: in a 比 sentence it means even more, often with surprise (今天比昨天还热); before 不错 or 可以 it means passably, not bad (这个饭馆的菜还不错).
越 (yuè) is used twice: 越 + verb + 越 + adjective says one thing grows with another: 他的汉语越说越好. The fixed phrase 越来越 (more and more) is taught with the fixed phrases.

The contrast example uses 最 (Level 2): 他跑得最快. 最 picks the top one in a group; 更 and 还 compare with one other thing. Common mistake: putting 很 or 非常 in a 比 sentence (今天比昨天很热). After 比 use 更 or 还, or nothing.

rows.label: 程度副词 (特别, 挺, 有些, 极)

lesson.title: Degree adverbs for strength: 特别, 挺, 有些 and 极
lesson.summary: 特别 means especially or particularly, 挺 is a spoken quite, 有些 means a bit (usually of something unwelcome), and 极 means extremely, before an adjective or in Adj + 极了.
pattern: A + 特别 / 挺 / 有些 / 极 + Adj / V
A + 挺 + Adj + 的
Adj + 极了；…，特别是 + N
body: 特别 (tèbié) means very or particularly: 他对我们特别好. 特别是 + noun picks out one member of a group: 我喜欢水果，特别是苹果. 挺 (tǐng) is spoken and means quite; it often has 的 at the end: 这本书挺有意思的.

有些 (yǒuxiē) as an adverb means a bit, like 有点儿, usually for something unwelcome: 我有些担心他. 极 (jí) means extremely. Before an adjective it is formal (这一点极重要); after an adjective, 极了 is spoken and strong: 好极了.

The contrast example uses 有些 as a pronoun (Level 1), meaning some: 有些人不喜欢吃辣的. Before a noun 有些 means some; before an adjective or verb it means a bit. Common mistake: putting 了 after 极 + adjective (极好了). Say 极好 or 好极了.

rows.label: 范围副词 (就, 一块儿, 一共, 只, 到处, 只是)

lesson.title: Scope adverbs: 就 (only), 一块儿, 一共, 只, 到处 and 只是
lesson.summary: 就 and 只 limit to only, 只是 means merely, 一共 adds up a total, 一块儿 means together, and 到处 means everywhere.
pattern: 就 + N / pronoun / number；A + 只 + V
A + 一共 + number / 多少
A + 一块儿 + V；到处 + 都 + …
body: 就 (jiù) can mean only and stands before a noun, a pronoun or a number: 今天就我一个人在家. 只 (zhǐ) means only and stands before the verb: 我只有一百块钱. 只是 (zhǐshì) means merely, just: 我只是问问. Between clauses 只是 can also mean it's just that, a soft but.
一共 (yígòng) means in total and goes with a number or 多少: 这些东西一共多少钱？ 一块儿 (yíkuàir) is a spoken word for together, like 一起: 咱们一块儿去爬山吧. 到处 (dàochù) means everywhere and usually goes with 都: 到处都是花.

The contrast example uses 都 (Level 1): 这些菜我都喜欢吃. 都 says each of the things mentioned before it; 一共 adds things up to a number, so it needs a number or 多少 after it. Common mistake: putting 只 before a subject (只我知道). Say 只有我知道 or 就我知道.

rows.label: 时间副词 (才, 马上, 先, 一会儿, 刚, 刚刚, 一直)

lesson.title: Time adverbs: 才, 马上, 先, 一会儿, 刚, 刚刚 and 一直
lesson.summary: 才 says later than expected, 马上 right away, 先 first, 一会儿 in a moment, 刚 and 刚刚 just now, and 一直 all along.
pattern: A + time + 才 + V
A + 马上 / 一会儿 + (就) + V
A + 刚 / 刚刚 / 一直 / 先 + V
body: 才 (cái) after a time word says the action happened later than expected: 他七点半才到. 马上 (mǎshàng) means right away, often with 就 or 就要: 电影马上就要开始了. 先 (xiān) means first: 你先坐一下. 一会儿 (yíhuìr) before a verb means in a moment: 我一会儿就来; after a verb it means for a while.

刚 (gāng) and 刚刚 (gānggāng) mean just, a very short time ago: 我刚到家. 刚 is an adverb and stays after the subject; 刚刚 can also be a time word and stand before the subject: 刚刚你去哪儿了？ 一直 (yìzhí) means continuously, all along: 雨一直下了三天.

The contrast example uses 已经 (Level 2): 我们已经认识很多年了. 已经 says a point has been reached, however long ago; 刚 says something happened only a moment ago, so it cannot go with 很多年. Common mistake: ending a 刚 sentence with 了 (我刚到家了). Say 我刚到家.

rows.label: 频率副词 (总, 总是, 又, 常常)

lesson.title: Frequency adverbs: 总, 总是, 常常 and 又
lesson.summary: 总 and 总是 mean always, 常常 means often, and 又 means again for something that has happened or that comes round regularly.
pattern: A + 总 / 总是 / 常常 + V
A + 又 + V + 了
又 + 是 + time + 了
body: 总 (zǒng) and 总是 (zǒngshì) mean always, every time: 他总是忘带钥匙, 周末他总在家看书. 总 is shorter and more spoken. 常常 (chángcháng) means often, less than always: 我常常跟朋友一起去游泳. Its negative is 不常.
又 (yòu) means again for something that has already happened, usually with 了: 他昨天又迟到了. It is also used for something that comes round regularly: 明天又是星期一了.

The contrast example uses 再 (Level 1): 我想再看一遍. 再 is again for something that has not happened yet; 又 is again for something that has. Common mistake: using 又 for a future wish (我想又看一遍) or 再 for a past event (他昨天再迟到了).

rows.label: 关联副词 (一边)

lesson.title: 一边……一边……: doing two things at once
lesson.summary: 一边 before each of two verbs says one person does both actions at the same time.
pattern: A + 一边 + V1 (+ O)，一边 + V2 (+ O)
A + 边 + V1 + 边 + V2
body: 一边 (yìbiān) is used in pairs: 一边 + verb, 一边 + verb. It says one subject does two actions at the same time: 他一边听音乐，一边写作业. Both verbs must be actions that last for a while, such as 听, 看, 走, 唱, 聊. With one-syllable verbs and no objects, speech often shortens it to 边走边聊.
The contrast example uses 着 (Level 2) between two verbs: 孩子们唱着歌回家了. With V1 + 着 + V2 the first action is only the manner of the main one; with 一边……一边…… the two actions have equal weight.
Common mistake: using 一边 with two different subjects (我一边做饭，他一边看电视) or with an action that is over in a moment (一边到, 一边开门). Use 一边……一边…… for one person and two lasting actions.

rows.label: 情态副词 (大概, 必须, 差不多, 一定, 好像, 几乎)

lesson.title: Adverbs of likelihood and necessity: 大概, 必须, 差不多, 一定, 好像, 几乎
lesson.summary: 大概 means probably, 必须 must, 差不多 about the same or almost, 一定 certainly, 好像 seems, and 几乎 almost.
pattern: A + 大概 / 好像 / 一定 + V
A + 必须 + V
A + 差不多；A + 几乎 + 没 / 每…
body: 大概 (dàgài) means probably: 他大概已经到家了. 好像 (hǎoxiàng) means it seems: 外面好像下雨了. 一定 (yídìng) means certainly; with a person's plan it is a promise (我一定来), and with a guess it means must be (他一定很累了). 必须 (bìxū) means must, have to: 开车的时候必须小心. Its negative is 不用 or 不必, never 不必须.
差不多 (chàbuduō) as a predicate means about the same: 颜色差不多; before a verb it means almost: 饭差不多做好了. 几乎 (jīhū) means almost, nearly, and often goes with 没 or 每: 他几乎没吃东西.

The contrast example uses 可能 (Level 2): 明天可能会下雨. 可能 says something may happen; 必须 says it has to, and 几乎 says it nearly did. Common mistake: using 差不多 or 几乎 as a guess about the future (我差不多明天来). Use 大概 or 可能.

rows.label: 语气副词 (当然, 其实, 终于, 才, 就)

lesson.title: Attitude adverbs: 当然, 其实, 终于, emphatic 才 and 就
lesson.summary: 当然 means of course, 其实 actually, 终于 at last; 才 can mean only (a small amount) or stress a strong denial, and 就 can stress that something is exactly so.
pattern: A + 当然 / 其实 / 终于 + V
才 + number；A + 才 + 不 + V + 呢；这才是…
A + 就 + 在 / 是…
body: 当然 (dāngrán) means of course: 你当然要帮他. 其实 (qíshí) means actually, in fact, and corrects what people think: 其实他是日本人. 终于 (zhōngyú) means at last, after a long wait: 车终于来了.

才 (cái) has two attitude uses. Before a number it means only, a small amount: 现在才七点. In 才不……呢 or 这才是 it stresses the speaker's view strongly: 我才不相信他的话呢, 这才是真正的朋友. 就 (jiù) can stress that something is exactly so or very near: 我家就在学校旁边.

The contrast example uses 就 as a link between clauses (Level 2): 你不去，我就一个人去. That 就 means then, in that case; the attitude 就 stresses a fact. Common mistake: using 终于 for something that came quickly. 终于 needs a wait or an effort before it.

examples.text: 他是你的朋友，你当然要帮他。
examples.reading: tā shì nǐ de péngyou, nǐ dāngrán yào bāng tā.
examples.translation: He's your friend; of course you should help him.

examples.text: 大家都以为他是中国人，其实他是日本人。
examples.reading: dàjiā dōu yǐwéi tā shì Zhōngguó rén, qíshí tā shì Rìběn rén.
examples.translation: Everyone thought he was Chinese, but actually he is Japanese.

examples.text: 等了一个小时，车终于来了。
examples.reading: děng le yí ge xiǎoshí, chē zhōngyú lái le.
examples.translation: After an hour's wait the bus finally came.

examples.text: 现在才七点，你再睡一会儿吧。
examples.reading: xiànzài cái qī diǎn, nǐ zài shuì yíhuìr ba.
examples.translation: It's only seven; sleep a bit longer.

examples.reading: wǒ cái bù xiāngxìn tā de huà ne!
examples.translation: I don't believe a word he says!

examples.reading: zhè cái shì zhēnzhèng de péngyou.
examples.translation: Now that is a true friend.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā jiù zài xuéxiào pángbiān.
examples.translation: My home is right next to the school.

examples.reading: nǐ bú qù, wǒ jiù yí ge rén qù.
examples.translation: If you won't go, I'll go on my own.

rows.label: 否定副词 (不必, 不用)

lesson.title: 不用 and 不必: there is no need to
lesson.summary: 不用 and 不必 both say there is no need; 不用 is spoken, 不必 a little more formal, and both are the negative of 必须, 得 and 要.
pattern: A + 不用 / 不必 + V
不用了 / 不必了
body: 不用 (búyòng) and 不必 (búbì) say something is not necessary: 你不用担心, 大家不必等我. 不用 is the everyday spoken form; 不必 is slightly more formal. Either can stand alone with 了 to turn down an offer politely: 不用了，谢谢.
They are the negative of 必须 (must), 得 (děi, have to) and 要 (need to): 明天不用上班. The negative of 必须 is never 不必须.

The contrast example uses 别 (Level 2): 你别忘了带钥匙. 别 forbids or warns (don't); 不用 and 不必 only say there is no need, and nobody ever needs to forget, so 你不用忘了 makes no sense. Common mistake: saying 不必须 for no need.

examples.text: 你不用担心，我自己能去。
examples.reading: nǐ búyòng dānxīn, wǒ zìjǐ néng qù.
examples.translation: Don't worry; I can go by myself.

examples.reading: nǐ búbì wèi zhè jiàn shì zháojí.
examples.translation: There's no need for you to worry about this.

examples.reading: búyòng le, xièxie.
examples.translation: No need, thank you.

examples.reading: dàjiā búbì děng wǒ, xiān chī ba.
examples.translation: No need to wait for me, everyone; go ahead and eat.

examples.text: 明天是星期六，不用上班。
examples.reading: míngtiān shì xīngqīliù, búyòng shàngbān.
examples.translation: Tomorrow is Saturday, so there's no need to go to work.

examples.reading: nǐ bié wàng le dài yàoshi.
examples.translation: Don't forget to bring your keys.

rows.label: 介词: 引出对象 (为, 向, 关于)

lesson.title: 为, 向 and 关于: for someone, to someone, about something
lesson.summary: 为 introduces the person who benefits, 向 the person an action is aimed at, and 关于 the topic something is about.
pattern: A + 为 + person + V
A + 向 + person + V
关于 + topic (+ 的 + N)；关于 + topic，…
body: 为 (wèi) introduces the person who benefits from an action, for: 妈妈为我们做了一桌子菜, 医生为病人看病. 向 (xiàng) introduces the person an action is directed at, to or from: 你应该向他学习, 他向大家介绍了自己的家乡.
关于 (guānyú) introduces a topic, about or concerning. It can go before 的 and a noun (一个关于长城的故事) or open a sentence with a comma (关于这件事，大家还有什么问题吗？).

The contrast example uses 对 (Level 1): 老师对学生很热情. 对 shows an attitude towards someone; 向 is for an action aimed at someone, 为 for a benefit and 关于 for a topic. Common mistake: using 关于 after the subject before a verb, as in 我关于这个问题有意见. Put 关于 at the start of the sentence or before 的 + noun, or use 对.

examples.text: 妈妈为我们做了一桌子菜。
examples.reading: māma wèi wǒmen zuò le yì zhuōzi cài.
examples.translation: Mum made a whole table of dishes for us.

examples.reading: nǐ yīnggāi xiàng tā xuéxí.
examples.translation: You should learn from him.

examples.text: 他向大家介绍了自己的家乡。
examples.reading: tā xiàng dàjiā jièshào le zìjǐ de jiāxiāng.
examples.translation: He told everyone about his hometown.

examples.text: 他给我们讲了一个关于长城的故事。
examples.reading: tā gěi wǒmen jiǎng le yí ge guānyú Chángchéng de gùshi.
examples.translation: He told us a story about the Great Wall.

examples.text: 关于这件事，大家还有什么问题吗？
examples.reading: guānyú zhè jiàn shì, dàjiā hái yǒu shénme wèntí ma?
examples.translation: Does anyone have any other questions about this?

examples.reading: yīshēng wèi bìngrén kànbìng.
examples.translation: The doctor treats the patients.

examples.reading: lǎoshī duì xuéshēng hěn rèqíng.
examples.translation: The teacher is very warm towards the students.

rows.label: 介词: 引出方向、路径 (向)

lesson.title: 向 for direction: towards a direction, a place or a person
lesson.summary: 向 before a direction word or a person says which way an action goes; in writing it can also follow a verb of motion, as in 飞向.
pattern: 向 + 前 / 后 / 左 / 右 / 东… + V
向 + person + V (+ 过来 / 过去)
V + 向 + place (written)
body: 向 (xiàng) says which way an action goes. Before a direction word it works like 往 (Level 2): 一直向前走, 向右转, 河水向东流. In writing it can follow a one-syllable verb of motion: 飞向北京, 走向门口.
向 can also take a person as the target of a movement: 他向我走过来. 往 is most natural with a place or a direction word, so with a person say 往我这儿走; 向 or 朝 takes the person directly.
The contrast example uses 从 (Level 2): 我们从这个门进去吧. 从 marks the starting point or the route; 向 marks the direction of the movement. Common mistake: using 在 for direction (在右转). Say 向右转 or 往右转.

examples.reading: yìzhí xiàng qián zǒu jiù dào le.
examples.translation: Go straight ahead and you'll be there.

examples.reading: dào le lùkǒu xiàng yòu zhuǎn.
examples.translation: Turn right when you reach the crossing.

examples.reading: héshuǐ xiàng dōng liú.
examples.translation: The river flows east.

examples.reading: fēijī fēi xiàng Běijīng.
examples.translation: The plane is flying towards Beijing.

examples.reading: tā xiàng wǒ zǒu guòlai.
examples.translation: He walked over towards me.

examples.reading: wǒmen cóng zhège mén jìnqu ba.
examples.translation: Let's go in through this door.

rows.label: 介词: 引出目的、原因 (为了, 为)

lesson.title: 为了 and 为: for a purpose, because of a cause
lesson.summary: 为了 introduces a purpose, in order to or for the sake of; 为 introduces the cause of a feeling, as in 为你高兴.
pattern: 为了 + purpose，A + V
A + 是为了 + purpose
A + 为 + cause + 高兴 / 着急 / 生气
body: 为了 (wèile) introduces a purpose: in order to, for the sake of. It can open the sentence (为了学好汉语，他每天听中文歌) or follow 是 at the end (他跑步是为了身体健康). It can take a verb phrase or a noun: 为了孩子.
为 (wèi) can introduce the cause of a feeling, with verbs such as 高兴, 着急, 担心 and 生气: 大家都为你感到高兴, 别为这点儿小事生气.

The contrast example uses 因为 (Level 2): 因为感冒了，他没去上班. 因为 gives a reason that already exists; 为了 gives a goal. Nobody catches a cold on purpose, so 为了感冒了 is wrong. Common mistake: using 为了 for a cause (为了下雨，我们没去). Use 因为.

examples.text: 为了学好汉语，他每天听中文歌。
examples.reading: wèile xuéhǎo Hànyǔ, tā měitiān tīng Zhōngwén gē.
examples.translation: He listens to Chinese songs every day to learn Chinese well.

examples.reading: tā zhèyàng zuò dōu shì wèile nǐ.
examples.translation: He is doing all this for you.

examples.reading: dàjiā dōu wèi nǐ gǎndào gāoxìng.
examples.translation: Everyone is happy for you.

examples.reading: bié wèi zhè diǎnr xiǎo shì shēngqì.
examples.translation: Don't get angry over such a small thing.

examples.text: 为了孩子，她换了一份离家近的工作。
examples.reading: wèile háizi, tā huàn le yí fèn lí jiā jìn de gōngzuò.
examples.translation: For her child's sake, she changed to a job close to home.

examples.text: 他跑步是为了身体健康。
examples.reading: tā pǎobù shì wèile shēntǐ jiànkāng.
examples.translation: He runs to stay healthy.

examples.text: 因为感冒了，他没去上班。
examples.reading: yīnwèi gǎnmào le, tā méi qù shàngbān.
examples.translation: He didn't go to work because he had a cold.

rows.label: 介词: 引出施事、受事 (把, 被)

lesson.title: 把 and 被: bringing the object forward, naming the doer
lesson.summary: 把 puts the object before the verb to say what is done to it; 被 makes the affected thing the subject and names the doer after 被.
pattern: A + 把 + O + V + extra (了 / 在… / 给… / result)
O + 被 + (doer) + V + extra
body: 把 (bǎ) brings the object in front of the verb to say what happens to it: 请把门关上, 我把作业忘在家里了, 你把这本书带给他吧. The verb cannot stand alone; it needs something after it, such as a result (关上), a place (在家里) or a receiver (给他).

被 (bèi) turns the sentence round: the thing affected becomes the subject, and the doer follows 被: 他被老师批评了, 蛋糕被弟弟吃完了. The doer can be a vague 人: 我的自行车被人借走了. 被 sentences often describe something unwelcome. Negatives and modal verbs go before 把 and 被: 没把, 不能被.

The contrast example uses 给 (Level 2): 他给朋友打了一个电话. 给 introduces the person who receives something; it does not move the object or mark a doer. Common mistake: a bare verb after 把 or 被 (我把书看). Add a result or 了: 我把书看完了.

examples.reading: qǐng bǎ mén guānshang.
examples.translation: Please shut the door.

examples.reading: wǒ bǎ zuòyè wàng zài jiā li le.
examples.translation: I left my homework at home.

examples.text: 我的自行车被人借走了。
examples.reading: wǒ de zìxíngchē bèi rén jiè zǒu le.
examples.translation: Someone has borrowed my bike.

examples.reading: tā bèi lǎoshī pīpíng le.
examples.translation: He was told off by the teacher.

examples.reading: dàngāo bèi dìdi chī wán le.
examples.translation: The cake has been eaten up by my little brother.

examples.reading: nǐ bǎ zhè běn shū dài gěi tā ba.
examples.translation: Take this book to him, will you?

examples.text: 他给朋友打了一个电话。
examples.reading: tā gěi péngyou dǎ le yí ge diànhuà.
examples.translation: He gave his friend a call.

rows.label: 介词: 引出凭借、依据 (根据)

lesson.title: 根据: according to, on the basis of
lesson.summary: 根据 introduces the basis for a statement or a decision, according to; as a noun it means grounds or basis.
pattern: 根据 + basis，A + V
A + 根据 + basis + V
有 / 没有 + 根据
body: 根据 (gēnjù) introduces the information or rule something is based on: 根据这张地图，前面就是火车站. It can open the sentence with a comma or follow the subject before the verb: 老师根据我们的水平分了班, 我们要根据自己的情况来选择. It often appears in 是根据……的: 这个电影是根据他自己的故事拍的.
根据 is also a noun meaning grounds, evidence: 你这么说有什么根据？

The contrast example uses 关于 (row 20): 一本关于熊猫的书. 关于 gives the topic, what the book is about; 根据 gives the source or basis, what something follows. Common mistake: using 关于 for a basis (关于这张地图，前面就是火车站). Use 根据.

examples.text: 根据这张地图，前面就是火车站。
examples.reading: gēnjù zhè zhāng dìtú, qiánmian jiù shì huǒchēzhàn.
examples.translation: According to this map, the railway station is just ahead.

examples.text: 我们要根据自己的情况来选择。
examples.reading: wǒmen yào gēnjù zìjǐ de qíngkuàng lái xuǎnzé.
examples.translation: We should choose according to our own situation.

examples.text: 这个电影是根据他自己的故事拍的。
examples.reading: zhège diànyǐng shì gēnjù tā zìjǐ de gùshi pāi de.
examples.translation: This film is based on his own story.

examples.reading: nǐ zhème shuō yǒu shénme gēnjù?
examples.translation: What grounds do you have for saying that?

examples.text: 老师根据我们的水平分了班。
examples.reading: lǎoshī gēnjù wǒmen de shuǐpíng fēn le bān.
examples.translation: The teacher divided us into classes by level.

examples.text: 这是一本关于熊猫的书。
examples.reading: zhè shì yì běn guānyú xióngmāo de shū.
examples.translation: This is a book about pandas.

rows.label: 连词: 连接词或短语 (或, 或者)

lesson.title: 或 and 或者: or, in statements
lesson.summary: 或者 and its shorter written form 或 join two choices in a statement; in a question that asks the listener to choose, use 还是.
pattern: A + 或者 / 或 + B
A 或者 B + 都 + 可以 / 行
question: A + 还是 + B？
body: 或者 (huòzhě) joins two choices, either of which is possible, in a statement: 你可以坐地铁或者坐公共汽车去. It can join nouns, verb phrases or whole clauses: 你可以给王老师打电话，或者给他发电子邮件. 或 (huò) is the shorter, more written form, often between two short words: 星期六或星期天.
With 都 after it the sentence says any of the choices is fine: 喝茶或者喝咖啡都可以.

The contrast example uses 还是 (Level 2) in a question: 你今天去还是明天去呢？ 还是 asks the listener to pick one; 或者 only lists options in a statement. Common mistake: using 或者 in a choice question (你喝茶或者喝咖啡？). Use 还是.

examples.text: 你可以坐地铁或者坐公共汽车去。
examples.reading: nǐ kěyǐ zuò dìtiě huòzhě zuò gōnggòng qìchē qù.
examples.translation: You can go by underground or by bus.

examples.text: 你可以给王老师打电话，或者给他发电子邮件。
examples.reading: nǐ kěyǐ gěi Wáng lǎoshī dǎ diànhuà, huòzhě gěi tā fā diànzǐ yóujiàn.
examples.translation: You can phone Mr Wang or send him an email.

examples.text: 我们星期六或星期天去看你。
examples.reading: wǒmen xīngqīliù huò xīngqītiān qù kàn nǐ.
examples.translation: We'll come and see you on Saturday or Sunday.

examples.text: 喝茶或者喝咖啡都可以。
examples.reading: hē chá huòzhě hē kāfēi dōu kěyǐ.
examples.translation: Tea or coffee, either is fine.

examples.text: 这本书你可以借，或者买一本。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū nǐ kěyǐ jiè, huòzhě mǎi yì běn.
examples.translation: You can borrow this book, or buy a copy.

examples.text: 你今天去还是明天去呢？
examples.reading: nǐ jīntiān qù háishi míngtiān qù ne?
examples.translation: Are you going today or tomorrow?

rows.label: 连词: 连接分句 (只有, 只要, 如果)

lesson.title: 只要, 只有 and 如果: conditions between clauses
lesson.summary: 只要 gives a condition that is enough (with 就), 只有 gives the only condition that works (with 才), and 如果 gives a supposition (with 就).
pattern: 只要 + condition，(A) + 就 + result
只有 + condition，(A) + 才 + result
如果 + supposition，(A) + 就 + result
body: 只要 (zhǐyào) says the condition is enough, as long as; the result clause takes 就: 只要你努力，就一定能学好. 只有 (zhǐyǒu) says this is the only condition that works, only if; the result clause takes 才: 只有多练习，才能说得好, 只有周末，我们才有时间一起吃饭.
如果 (rúguǒ) introduces a supposition, if; the result clause often takes 就: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了. 如果 can be followed by ……的话 at the end of its clause.
The contrast example uses 因为……所以…… (Level 2): 因为下大雪，所以学校今天放假. 因为 gives a real cause, not a condition. Common mistake: mixing the pairs (只有……就, 只要……才). Keep 只要 with 就 and 只有 with 才.

examples.text: 只要你努力，就一定能学好。
examples.reading: zhǐyào nǐ nǔlì, jiù yídìng néng xuéhǎo.
examples.translation: As long as you work hard, you will learn it well.

examples.text: 只有多练习，才能说得好。
examples.reading: zhǐyǒu duō liànxí, cái néng shuō de hǎo.
examples.translation: Only with plenty of practice can you speak well.

examples.text: 只要有时间，我就去看你。
examples.reading: zhǐyào yǒu shíjiān, wǒ jiù qù kàn nǐ.
examples.translation: Whenever I have time, I'll come and see you.

examples.text: 只有周末，我们才有时间一起吃饭。
examples.reading: zhǐyǒu zhōumò, wǒmen cái yǒu shíjiān yìqǐ chī fàn.
examples.translation: Only at weekends do we have time to eat together.

examples.text: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了。
examples.reading: rúguǒ míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù le.
examples.translation: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

examples.text: 因为下大雪，所以学校今天放假。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià dà xuě, suǒyǐ xuéxiào jīntiān fàngjià.
examples.translation: Because of the heavy snow, the school is closed today.

rows.label: 连词: 连接分句 (不但, 而且, 可, 可是, 然后)

lesson.title: 不但……而且, 可/可是 and 然后: adding, contrasting and sequencing clauses
lesson.summary: 不但……而且 adds a further point, 可是 and the shorter 可 turn to a contrast, and 然后 says what happens next.
pattern: A + 不但 + X，而且 + Y
X，可是 / 可 + Y
X，然后 + Y
body: 不但 (búdàn) … 而且 (érqiě) … means not only … but also: 我哥哥不但会做饭，而且做得很好吃. 而且 can also be used alone to add a point. 可是 (kěshì) means but, like 但是: 我很想去，可是没有时间. 可 (kě) is a shorter spoken form and stands after the subject or at the start of the clause: 他说今天来，可到现在也没来.
然后 (ránhòu) means then, afterwards, and links actions in time order: 下了课我去图书馆，然后回家. It often follows a first step with 先 in the first clause.

The contrast example uses 也 (Level 1): 他会唱歌，也会跳舞. 也 simply adds a similar fact; 不但……而且 adds a stronger or further point, and 然后 adds a later action, not a second fact. Common mistake: using 然后 for and in a list of facts (他很高，然后很帅). Use 而且 or 也.

examples.text: 我哥哥不但会做饭，而且做得很好吃。
examples.reading: wǒ gēge búdàn huì zuò fàn, érqiě zuò de hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: My elder brother not only can cook, his cooking is delicious.

examples.text: 这家饭馆的菜不但便宜，而且好吃。
examples.reading: zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài búdàn piányi, érqiě hǎochī.
examples.translation: The food at this restaurant is not only cheap but also tasty.

examples.text: 我很想去，可是没有时间。
examples.reading: wǒ hěn xiǎng qù, kěshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.translation: I'd love to go, but I don't have time.

examples.text: 他说今天来，可到现在也没来。
examples.reading: tā shuō jīntiān lái, kě dào xiànzài yě méi lái.
examples.translation: He said he'd come today, but he still hasn't.

examples.text: 下了课我去图书馆，然后回家。
examples.reading: xià le kè wǒ qù túshūguǎn, ránhòu huí jiā.
examples.translation: After class I go to the library and then home.

examples.text: 他起床以后喝了一杯水，然后去跑步了。
examples.reading: tā qǐchuáng yǐhòu hē le yì bēi shuǐ, ránhòu qù pǎobù le.
examples.translation: After getting up he drank a glass of water, then went running.

examples.reading: tā huì chàng gē, yě huì tiàowǔ.
examples.translation: He can sing, and he can dance too.

rows.label: 助词 (的话)

lesson.title: ……的话: if, at the end of a condition
lesson.summary: 的话 closes a condition clause and means if; it can be used alone or together with 如果 at the start.
pattern: condition + 的话，(A) + (就) + result
如果 + condition + 的话，…
body: 的话 (de huà) goes at the end of a clause and makes it a condition: 明天下雨的话，我们就在家看电影, 有时间的话，来我家玩儿吧. The result clause often has 就. 的话 is common in speech and can be used alone or with 如果 at the start: 如果你有问题的话，可以问我.
The contrast example uses 的时候 (Level 2): 我到家的时候，妈妈正在做饭. 的时候 says when something really happened; 的话 says if something happens. A real past event takes 的时候, not 的话.
Common mistake: putting 的话 at the start of the clause (的话明天下雨). It always comes at the end of the condition, before the comma.

examples.text: 明天下雨的话，我们就在家看电影。
examples.reading: míngtiān xià yǔ de huà, wǒmen jiù zài jiā kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: If it rains tomorrow, we'll watch a film at home.

examples.text: 如果你有问题的话，可以问我。

examples.translation: If you have any questions, you can ask me.

examples.text: 你不想去的话，就别去了。
examples.reading: nǐ bù xiǎng qù de huà, jiù bié qù le.
examples.translation: If you don't want to go, then don't.

examples.text: 有时间的话，来我家玩儿吧。
examples.reading: yǒu shíjiān de huà, lái wǒ jiā wánr ba.

examples.translation: If you're not feeling well, take the day off.

examples.translation: When I got home, Mum was cooking.

lesson.title: More phrase types: appositives, 得/不 complements and doubled number-measures
lesson.summary: An appositive phrase puts two names for the same thing side by side (我们俩); a verb can take 得 or 不 before its complement (听不懂); and a doubled number + measure (一个一个) means one after another.
pattern: pronoun + 俩 / number + 个 / 大家；N + name (首都北京)
V + 得 / 不 + complement
一 + M + 一 + M (+ 地) + V
body: In an appositive phrase two parts name the same people or thing: 我们俩, 你们两个, 他们大家, 首都北京, 我的朋友小王. 俩 (liǎ) already means two people, so it never takes 个.

Verb-complement phrases at this level put 得 or 不 between the verb and its complement to say can or cannot (听得懂, 听不懂), or put 得 before a description of how the action turned out (说得太快, 写得很漂亮). A doubled number + measure means one after another, step by step: 一个一个进来, 一口一口地喝, 一天一天长大.

The contrast example uses 个个 (row 11): 这些苹果个个都很甜. A doubled measure without a number means every one, all of them; 一个一个 with the number describes the manner, one at a time. Common mistake: 我们俩个. Say 我们俩 or 我们两个.

examples.reading: wǒmen liǎ shì hǎo péngyou.
examples.translation: The two of us are good friends.

examples.reading: nǐmen liǎng ge gēn wǒ lái.
examples.translation: You two, come with me.

examples.reading: tāmen dàjiā dōu tóngyì le.

examples.text: 老师说得太快，我听不懂。

examples.translation: Please come in one at a time, everyone.

examples.text: 他一口一口地把药喝完了。
examples.reading: tā yì kǒu yì kǒu de bǎ yào hē wán le.
examples.translation: He drank the medicine down mouthful by mouthful.

examples.reading: zhèxiē píngguǒ gègè dōu hěn tián.
examples.translation: Every one of these apples is sweet.
